newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cement, mills take Egyptian shares to new high.
newsitem.headline: Cement, mills take Egyptian shares to new high.

text.p: Egyptian shares surged 2.8 percent to a third straight record high on Tuesday on strong gains especially in the cement and milling sectors.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index closed 9.54 points up at 346.58 on above average turnover of 66.57 million pounds ($19.6 million), the CMA said.
Brokers say foreign buying is the biggest single factor behind the rise in share prices, which on average have gained 20.7 percent in the past month and 64.4 percent in a year.
The boom has continued right into the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan, despite shorter working hours at the exchange.
The cement shares seemed the main attraction on Tuesday, led by Amriyah Cement, which accounted for trade worth more than 11 million pounds. It closed 6.50 pounds up at 77.50.
Helwan Portland Cement jumped 7.00 to 77.00, Egyptian Tora Portland Cement gained 6.50 to 95.00 and Alexandria Portland Cement rose 5.95 to 65.45..
Milling shares, all of them partially privatised since the middle of last year, rose in lower volume than cements.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed the day at 84.00, from 79.00 on Monday, and South Cairo Flour Mills at 85.00 pounds, up from 83.00.

Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceuticals stood out in the pharmaceutical sector, gaining 10.00 to 190.00 in several big transactions. Brokers said on Monday they thought the government-run holding company was selling part of its stake in the firm through the stock exchange.
Popular real estate company Medinet Nasr Housing and Development slipped 0.25 to 418.25 in busy trade.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 557.95 from 544.32 points on Monday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 233.83 from 226.92.
Of the 69 shares traded, 41 gained, 18 lost and 10 ended the day unchanged.
